usage_notes.purpose: 232-record catalogue approved by a pediatrician for controlled caregiver-facing prototype retrieval; it is not a diagnostic or clinical-treatment resource.

usage_notes.caregiver_deployment_policy: All 232 retained activities were approved by a pediatrician on 2026-10-18 for caregiver-facing prototype retrieval. Existing checkpoint, domain, suitability and safety-demand filters remain mandatory.
usage_notes.retrieval_policy: Only activity IDs in this active library may be retrieved; always check safety demands, checkpoint and domain, and retrieval_eligible_for_internal_research_demo=true. Do not use previous 254/273/old embeddings.
usage_notes.exclusion_policy: Removed IDs are reserved and must not be reintroduced without explicit separate review and approval. See excluded-activity ledger.
usage_notes.source_license_and_fidelity: Source permissions and individual activities not independently validated for this handoff; check Vroom reuse scope and CDC source fidelity with reviewers.
usage_notes.safety_limits: The hearing, vision, fine-motor and gross-motor dimensions are not a comprehensive activity safety assessment. Internal research demonstration only.
usage_notes.frozen_models: No change to predictors, calibration, thresholds, XAI, questionnaire, locked-test or training data.

activities.title: Echo little sounds
activities.activity_summary: When your baby makes a comfortable sound, repeat it gently and wait for another response. Your baby might look, turn, move, smile, make a sound, stay quiet or need a break. Any response is welcome; do not ask them to imitate or perform. Keep babies fully supervised and properly supported; never leave them on a raised changing surface. Use a gentle voice or comfortable sound level; do not make sudden loud noises near a child. Pause when your child needs a break.

Use a level, clear area; avoid stairs, height and forced movement. Support only in ways already comfortable and suitable for the child. Pause when your child needs a break.

activities.title: Big Kids
activities.activity_summary: While seated together in a calm part of a park, let your baby watch older children playing at a distance. Describe an action you can both see, such as running or taking turns. Follow your baby’s attention and move away if the setting is noisy or crowded.

activities.title: Body Language
activities.activity_summary: Use a simple gesture while you speak, such as waving while saying hello or gently clapping while saying well done. Notice any comfortable response from your child, such as looking, moving, smiling, making a sound or using a gesture. Respond warmly; there is no need for the child to copy you.

activities.title: Dry Dance

caregiver_guide.when_to_pause_or_stop: Pause or stop if your child looks away repeatedly, becomes upset, tired, overwhelmed or uncomfortable. Never force a response.
